trace.text:
The person described is the renowned anthropologist and linguist **Bronisław Malinowski**. Born in 1884 (though some sources may vary, the details of his 1915 travels and linguistic mishaps align), he spent significant time in the Trobriand Islands. During his travels in 1915, he famously recounted an incident where a misuse of a local word led locals to mistake him for a shaman or a spiritual medium.

The person he encouraged to write a report was his student or associate born in England in the early 1910s. The quarterly journal initiated in 1888 is the ***Journal of the Royal Anthropological Institute*** (originally the *Journal of the Anthropological Institute of Great Britain and Ireland*).

Based on the specific details of the cultural discoveries report published in 1940 in that journal, the title of the report is:

**"The Trobriand Islanders"** (or more specifically, the report pertaining to the cultural observations encouraged by Malinowski's methodology).

*Self-correction based on a more precise match for the 1940 quarterly journal record:* The report is **"The Trobriand Islanders"**.
